title: Growth in International Passenger Numbers at Changi Airport
what_it_is: Growth in International Passenger Numbers at Changi Airport

sections.label: Airport passenger growth rates
sections.summary: Overseas visitors arriving by air in Singapore grew at a 4.1% CAGR, while Bangkok, Kuala Lumpur and Jakarta airports had five-year CAGRs of 10.2%, 7.4% and 3.5%.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: In the same period, the number of overseas visitors who came to Singapore by air grew at a CAGR of 4.1%.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The five-year CAGR for international passengers handled at the Bangkok, Kuala Lumpur and Jakarta airports were 10.2%, 7.4% and 3.5% for the period 2011 to 2016, based on publicly available full-year data.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: We do not have data on the number of overseas visitors the three foreign airports handled.

sections.label: Changi as premier air hub
sections.summary: Bangkok's two airports and domestic LCC growth gave it 10.2% growth, while Jakarta started from a lower base; Changi will be anchored as a premier air hub, including building T5.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Bangkok and Singapore Changi Airport are at about the same base but, in Bangkok, they have two different airports to serve the domestic and the international market at Don Muang and Suvarnabhumi Airports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: With this advantage and also the domestic growth of LCCs, they have a 10.2% growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Whereas for Jakarta, it starts at a lower base, much lower numbers of passengers per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Nevertheless, what we want to do for Changi is to anchor it as a premier air hub, as we have done for so many years, which, also in time to come, will involve building a T5 for the expanded capacities to handle increased projected volumes of passengers.
